q: A matrix A is called positive definite if for all nonzero x: xᵀAx > 0. Equivalently, for symmetric A, this holds iff:
opts: A = BᵀB for some invertible B (Cholesky decomposition exists)
exp: Symmetric A is positive definite iff all eigenvalues are positive, iff A = LLᵀ for invertible lower-triangular L (Cholesky), iff all leading principal minors are positive (Sylvester's criterion). PD matrices define inner products and arise naturally in optimisation.
